title: Spur bench ticker - microbatch run log
body:
CSV: run_id,date,model,variant,batch_size,tokens_per_request,avg_latency_ms,p50_ms,p90_ms,p99_ms,cost_per_1k_tokens_usd,notes

R001,2026-03-01,redwood-open-l13,fp16,1,64,38,32,56,120,0.023,baseline single-request no cache
R002,2026-03-01,redwood-open-l13,fp16,4,64,45,40,70,150,0.016,gains from batching but tail increased
R003,2026-03-02,redwood-open-l13,quant8,4,64,33,28,52,95,0.011,quantized - much cheaper, p99 improved vs fp16 at same batch
R004,2026-03-04,redwood-open-l13,quant8,8,32,39,35,58,110,0.009,smaller tokens per request reduces batching efficiency
R005,2026-03-06,redwood-open-l13,fp16,1,256,120,110,200,400,0.080,long context - KV cache disabled for this run (control)
R006,2026-03-08,redwood-open-l13,fp16+kv,1,256,28,25,45,85,0.030,KV cache warm - big latency win vs R005
R007,2026-03-09,redwood-open-l13,quant8+kv,4,128,22,20,40,70,0.0075,aggressive quant + kv cache, cheapest per-token

Quick notes (scratch area):
- Primary goal: balance p99 <= 100ms for 256 token-ish requests while keeping cost <= $0.03/1k tokens for tier-1 customers.
- Observations: quant8 reduces avg latency and cost; p99 is sensitive to batch-size distribution (spiky small requests hurt tails).
- KV cache warm dramatically reduces end-to-end for long-context requests (compare R005 vs R006).
- Batching helps throughput but can worsen p99; consider continuous batching with latency SLO cutoff (max wait 8ms).

Next steps / TODO:
- (A) Re-run R007 with jittered arrival (simulate 80% small requests, 20% large) - see impact on p99 (ticket: ENG-1310).
- (B) Try quant16 (if available) to see quality/latency tradeoff. Quick PR: add quant16 profile to local runner.
- (C) Add token-level cost breakdown to the sheet (tokens spent on prompt vs generation).
- (D) Short experiment to enable KV sticky routing for repeat users (warm inference) - measure hit rate and cost delta.

Open questions / loose thoughts:
- Is the p99 we measure client-side or infra-side? Right now these are measured at the host process; need to correlate with gateway traces.
- Could autoscaling policy be made aware of batch formation state? e.g., if queue length > X spawn extra workers to keep p99 down.
- For Dedicated customers, we can push quant8 by default but need to prove output-quality parity on 200-sample eval set (low priority).

Quick math snippets: 
- Cost calc shorthand: (tokens_per_request * requests_per_min * 60) / 1000 * cost_per_1k_tokens_usd = USD/hr sample.
- Example: R007: assume 300 reqs/min * avg 128 tokens -> (128*300*60)/1000 * 0.0075 = $17.28/hr. (approx)

Scratch logs: 
- 2026-03-02 09:12 - toggled quant8 kernels on local venv; saw dropout of 0.3% in rare tokens.
- 2026-03-06 14:40 - manual KV preload script (tmp/preload.py) used to warm cache for tests.
